name: Mantua, 16 January 1797
description: Mantua and its lakes as they stood in the winter of 1796-97, drawn to 50 m a tile from the French siege plan of July 1796 and the surviving watercourses. The Mincio dams hold the Superiore, di Mezzo and Inferiore lakes; the drained Paiolo still rings the south of the fortress as a flooded ditch, and the Valli del Mincio reed marsh closes the west. Two causeways carry the only dry approaches - the Ponte dei Mulini under the guns of the Cittadella di Porto, and the Ponte di San Giorgio to the fortified borgo. The Migliaretto and Cerese hornworks cover the south front, French blockade redoubts ring the plain, and the Gonzaga villa of La Favorita stands in its walled park north of the lakes, where Provera's relief column was pinned and forced to surrender.
